meta.description: Daily tracking state for F-1/SEVP/DS-2019 policy monitoring, focused on relevance to a Virginia Tech student who may need an extra semester to finish their degree.

items.title: DHS Final Rule: Fixed Time Period of Admission & Extension of Stay (ends Duration of Status) for F, J, I nonimmigrants
items.summary: DHS published a final rule (doc. 2026-14439) on Jul 17, 2026, ending open-ended Duration of Status for F-1 students, effective Sep 15, 2026. Students get a fixed 'Admit Until Date' capped at 4 years (24 months for language programs); anyone needing more time must file Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) with USCIS in addition to the existing DSO SEVIS extension. A timely-filed EOS gives up to 240 days of authorized stay while pending. The rule also shortens the F-1 post-completion grace period from 60 to 30 days for anyone who travels/re-enters or gets an EOS approval after the effective date.
items.notes: No lawsuit had been filed and no Congressional Review Act disapproval resolution had passed as of this run (checked 2026-08-12); coverage still describes litigation/CRA action as 'possible' or 'expected,' not filed. NAFSA remains publicly opposed. SEVP has a stakeholder webinar reported for Mon, Aug 31, 2026, 2-3pm ET (per secondary reporting; studyinthestates.dhs.gov/webinars could not be fetched directly to independently confirm). New secondary-only detail surfaced today: multiple outlets (e.g. Forbes/Stuart Anderson, Aug 3, 2026) report DHS will not require an extension-of-stay filing during the first 6 months after the Sep 15, 2026 effective date for students applying for post-completion OPT/STEM OPT work authorization ('6-month transition reprieve') -- could not locate this specific provision in a directly-rendered official text today, so it stays a secondary-sourced detail, not upgraded to confirmed. Found likely-official DHS and ICE press-release URLs corroborating the rule via search (dhs.gov/news, ice.gov/news) but could not render them directly this run (network egress fully blocked, see sources section).

items.title: USCIS Policy Alert PA-2026-05: officers may deny incomplete filings without issuing an RFE/NOID first
items.summary: Effective Aug 5, 2026, USCIS updated Policy Manual guidance so adjudicators may, at their discretion, deny a benefit request lacking required initial evidence or failing to establish eligibility without first issuing an RFE or NOID, and may set RFE response deadlines shorter than the prior 12-week norm (the 14-day international-mail grace period was also eliminated). Directly relevant to F-1 students filing Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) or I-765 under the new fixed-admission-period regime: an incomplete EOS package can now be denied outright with no chance to cure.
items.notes: Could not reach uscis.gov/policy-manual directly again this run (all outbound network egress in this environment is currently blocked, confirmed via a Wikipedia control fetch failing too -- this is a total block, not a uscis.gov-specific one). Five to six independent law-firm sources continue to corroborate the exact Aug 5, 2026 effective date and mechanism with no contradicting reports, which is stronger-than-average secondary corroboration, but per the tracker's rule this stays 'Reported, unconfirmed' until an actual .gov page/PDF is rendered. Will keep retrying uscis.gov each run to move this to Confirmed.

items.title: DHS regulatory review of OPT / STEM OPT (RIN 1653-AA97) — no NPRM published yet
items.summary: DHS confirmed in a Jan 9, 2026 letter it is re-evaluating the scope and duration of OPT and STEM OPT, with a rulemaking entry (RIN 1653-AA97, titled 'Practical Training') in the Spring 2026 Unified Regulatory Agenda covering worker protection, fraud prevention, national security, and SEVP oversight goals. As of this run, no Notice of Proposed Rulemaking has been published in the Federal Register. A single secondary source (americanbazaaronline.com, Aug 11, 2026) newly reports the government's own unified agenda lists an NPRM target of February 2027 for this rule. OPT and STEM OPT remain fully operational and unchanged today. Relevant because many students planning an extra semester are also relying on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT timing.
items.notes: Could not reach reginfo.gov or federalregister.gov directly this run (blanket network egress block) to confirm the RIN 1653-AA97 unified-agenda entry text or the reported Feb 2027 NPRM target. No OPT/STEM OPT NPRM exists yet to cite as of 2026-08-12. Will keep watching for actual NPRM publication.

items.title: Reported $100,000 fee under consideration for OPT / post-completion work authorization
items.source: Press reporting (Forbes, Bloomberg, ICEF Monitor, The PIE News, Higher Ed Dive)
items.summary: Multiple outlets report the administration is weighing a $100,000 fee applicable to OPT employment authorization (and by extension STEM OPT), modeled on the now-struck-down $100,000 H-1B fee proclamation. As of the most recent reporting (Aug 11, 2026), immigration attorneys quoted say the fee is unlikely to survive legal challenge absent Congressional authorization, citing a June 8, 2026 district-court ruling and a July 24, 2026 appellate rejection of the administration's appeal in the analogous H-1B fee matter. Who would pay (student/university/employer) is unresolved, and DHS has not published a proposed rule or fee schedule. Directly relevant to students weighing an extra semester who are also counting on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT to work in the U.S. afterward.
items.notes: New item, first surfaced today via press reporting only. No DHS/USCIS/.gov statement or proposed rule found confirming or denying this. Could not reach dhs.gov or uscis.gov newsroom directly this run to check for an official statement (blanket network egress block). Related to but distinct from the RIN 1653-AA97 OPT/STEM OPT rulemaking review above -- reporting does not tie this fee proposal to that specific rulemaking docket.
